title: Zcash Supply Check
description: Checks the arithmetic of user-pasted Zcash chain value pool balances (transparent, Sprout, Sapling, Orchard, in integer zatoshi) against a claimed total supply: recomputes the pool sum exactly, checks every pool is non-negative (the pinned negative-balance consensus rules declare a negative pool an invalid chain state), and tests the no-counterfeiting conservation identity that the four pools together equal the claimed supply, reporting any difference exactly with its sign. It states plainly that it cannot read the chain and does not verify that the pasted numbers are true: evidence.chain_verified is false on every payload, including a conserved one. Refusal branches cover non-numeric values (never echoed), pool names outside the four pinned pools (lockbox included), a missing pool, an absent claimed supply, fractional zatoshi, and values above the declared safe-arithmetic bound. Declared exclusions: values only, no chain access, no lockbox or deferred pool, no height or issuance-history corroboration, no market or price figures, not investment advice.

pools.description: The four Zcash chain value pool balances in integer zatoshi, keyed transparent, sprout, sapling, orchard (the zcashd valuePools chainValueZat figures), pasted as a JSON object. All four pools must be present; a key outside the four pinned pool names is refused, never zeroed.

transparent.description: Transparent pool balance in integer zatoshi.

sprout.description: Sprout pool balance in integer zatoshi.

sapling.description: Sapling pool balance in integer zatoshi.

orchard.description: Orchard pool balance in integer zatoshi.

claimed_supply_zat.description: The claimed total supply the conservation identity is tested against, in integer zatoshi (the zcashd chainSupply chainValueZat figure). Absent, fractional, or over-bound values are refused, never assumed.

input_schema_provenance: Top-level properties are exactly the policy_parameters members the kernel reads: pools, claimed_supply_zat. No required array: the kernel itself refuses absent fields (claimed_supply_zat absent, a missing pinned pool) with structured refusal payloads, so the refusal branches stay reachable through every call path.
